The '''radian per second''' (symbol: '''rad⋅s<sup>−1</sup>''' or '''rad/s''') is the unit of [[angular velocity]] in the [[International System of Units]] (SI). The [[radian]] per [[second]] is also the SI unit of [[angular frequency]] (symbol ''ω'', omega). The radian per second is defined as the angular frequency that results in the [[angular displacement]] increasing by one radian every second.<ref>{{cite book |title=College Physics |publisher=OpenStax |url=https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/College_Physics/College_Physics_1e_(OpenStax)/06%3A_Uniform_Circular_Motion_and_Gravitation/6.01%3A_Rotation_Angle_and_Angular_Velocity |language=en |chapter=6.1: Rotation Angle and Angular Velocity|access-date=20 January 2024}}</ref>

==Relation to other units==
A [[frequency]] of one [[hertz]] (1&nbsp;Hz), or one [[cycle per second]] (1&nbsp;cps), corresponds to an angular frequency of 2{{pi}} radians per second. This is because one [[cycle (rotational unit)|cycle of rotation]] corresponds to an [[angle|angular]] rotation of 2{{pi}} radians.<ref>{{cite web |title=rpm to rad/s formula |url=https://convert.app/frequency/rpm-to-rads/ |website=convert.app |access-date=8 January 2026}}</ref> 

Since the radian is a [[dimensionless unit]] in the [[SI]], the radian per second is dimensionally equivalent to the hertz—both can be expressed as [[reciprocal seconds]], s<sup>−1</sup>. So, context is necessary to specify which [[kind of quantity]] is being expressed, angular frequency or ordinary frequency. 

One radian per second also corresponds to about 9.55 [[revolutions per minute]] (rpm).<ref>{{cite book |url=https://www.macquariedictionary.com.au/resources/view/resource/10/ | chapter=Metric Conversion: Language Resources |publisher=[[Macquarie Dictionary|Macquarie Dictionary Publishers]] |title=Macquarie Dictionary |via=[[National Library of Australia]] |archive-url=https://webarchive.nla.gov.au/awa/20160229064041/https://www.macquariedictionary.com.au/resources/view/resource/10/ |archive-date=29 February 2016 |access-date=27 January 2024 }}</ref> ''Degrees per second'' may also be defined, based on [[degrees (angle)|degree of arc]], where 1 degree per second (°/s) is equivalent to {{sfrac|{{pi}}|180}} rad⋅s<sup>−1</sup>.

== Coherent units ==
A use of the unit radian per second is in calculation of the power transmitted by a shaft. In the [[International System of Quantities]] (SI) and the [[International System of Units]], widely used in [[physics]] and [[engineering]], the power ''p'' is equal to the angular speed ''ω'' multiplied by the [[torque]] ''τ'' applied to the shaft: {{nowrap|1=''p'' = ''ω'' ⋅ ''τ''}}.  When [[Coherence (units of measurement)|coherent units]] are used for these quantities, which are respectively the [[watt]], the radian per second, and the [[newton-metre]], and thus {{nowrap|1=[[watt|W]] = rad/s × [[newton-metre|N·m]]}}, no numerical factor is needed when performing the numerical calculation. When the units are not coherent (e.g. [[horsepower]], [[turn (angle)|turn]]/min, and [[pound-foot (torque)|pound-foot]]), an additional factor will generally be necessary.
